rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Optional, non-blocking: a one-line maintainer note on either file documenting that the missing explicit-close instruction at the M5 end is deliberate (M5's run end-state is ambiguous by design; M6's rescue callout is the intended handling) -- a documentation nicety, not a student-facing gap.

spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md '## Start here' carries the two-callout rescue shape (nudge / re-send fresh / skip-opener; then accept-loss floor 'Despair not'), and the maintainer block explicitly documents it as a deliberate exception to check_student_facing.md rule 5, carve-out note present verbatim. Correctly scoped: M4->M5 does not need an equivalent rescue since any M4 outcome, even a one-minute stall, is valid material by design ('A stopped run counts; the trace is the artefact', 'Stopped, finished, ran out of credit, doesn't matter.') -- the starting-point commit that M5 forks from is written before the uncertain part of the run, so M5's fork point never depends on M4's task-execution actually succeeding. M6 genuinely needs 'substance' from M5, which is where the plausibly-thin-or-missing condition actually lives, so scoping the rescue to M6 only is correct, not an omission at M4->M5.

learn-from-the-test.md '## Bring to Module 6': 'Come to Module 6 without the packaged run and you'll be reading one run while the room is reading two. Your call.' Uses 'reading' rather than the sibling instances' 'scrambling', but satisfies the rule's binding test (plain-English, student-as-subject, choice-preserved, none of the three named failure modes present) -- a sharper M6-specific lexical variant, not a violation.
